name: Far-field Culling
definition: An optimization that replaces SDF trees in cells far from the 0-isosurface with a single constant node providing a lower-bound distance, speeding up conservative tasks like sphere tracing.
summary: Far-field culling optimizes SDF evaluation by replacing distant cells with constant lower-bound nodes, aggressively simplifying empty space to improve tracing performance where exact differentiability is not required.
